# Hydrostatic and well-balanced treatment {#sec-ch05}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md, hydrostatic and well-balanced treatment; docs/derivations/wb-ref4.md, wb-ref-wall.md, x1-centroid-spherical.md at the pin
status: draft
-->

A stratified atmosphere at rest is the state snapy's $x_1$[^rg-f764c1a0ef5d] sweep has to leave alone, and it is the hardest one:
its pressure and density change by orders of magnitude along $x_1$, while the motions of interest are small
perturbations of it. This chapter describes how the $x_1$ reconstruction keeps such a column at rest to round-off
and how close the reference it uses comes to the column's own profile. It covers, in the order the code builds
them: the well-balanced $x_1$ reconstruction, which reconstructs perturbations about a discretely hydrostatic
reference; the reference kernel, which builds that reference from a top-down pressure scan; its closure at a
physical wall; its continuity across $x_1$ block seams; the hydrostatic mode, which replaces gravity by the cell's
own pressure difference; `balance_column`, which projects an initial column onto the scheme's discrete balance;
the fourth-order reference `SNAP_WB_REF4`; the $r^2$-exact $x_1$ maps `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` of spherical-polar
grids; what is left of the $1/r$ term after them; and two legacy wall routines. The gravity work these schemes are
used with is @sec-ch06; the switches and their tested combinations are @sec-ch12.

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
All derivations of this chapter are checked by one executable check, `src/snapy_report/ch05/checks/wbref_check.py`,
whose output `wbref_check.out` carries the claim tags `[C1]`–`[C21]`; claim `[C11]` is an independent rebuild of
the default reference from the equations of this chapter that reproduces the numbers snapy's own wall test prints.
:::

| scheme | switch | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WB[^rg-cd3a4587f5d3] $x_1$ reconstruction (@sec-ch05-wbx1) | gravity on | on | rest exact | `test_face_floor` |
| Reference kernel (@sec-ch05-refkernel) | with the WB path | on | 2 ($\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$[^rg-db3b2c69533d]) | `test_hydro_ref_x1` |
| Wall clamp and continuation (@sec-ch05-wallclamp) | `wb-wall-clamp`[^rg-5826c2f5cd26] | on | 2 at walls | `test_wb_ref_wall` |
| Seam continuity (@sec-ch05-seam) | $x_1$ split | on | exact | `test_pref_local_seam` |
| Hydrostatic mode (@sec-ch05-hsmode) | `non-hydrostatic`[^rg-e659dcc78f19] | 1 (off) | rest exact | `test_hydrostatic` |
| `balance_column` (@sec-ch05-balcol) | API[^rg-f70527012078] call | not called | fixed point | `test_balance_column` |
| Fourth-order reference (@sec-ch05-wbref4) | `SNAP_WB_REF4` | off | 4 ($\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$) | `test_wb_ref4_order` |
| $r^2$-exact $x_1$ maps (@sec-ch05-x1cent) | `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` | off | rest exact | `test_x1_centroid_rest` |
| $1/r$ remainder (@sec-ch05-oneoverr) | none | — | $O(\Delta x_1^2/r)$ | none |
| Legacy wall routines (@sec-ch05-legacy) | none | unreachable | — | none |

: The schemes of this chapter. "Order" is the order of the face density reference $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}$ against the
exact profile where a number is given; "rest exact" means a discretely balanced column stays at rest to round-off.
Full ctest names and tolerances are in each scheme's Tests layer and in the chapter's entry of the verification catalogue. {#tbl-ch05-schemes}

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-f764c1a0ef5d]: $x_1, x_2, x_3$ — the three coordinate directions; $x_1$ is always the vertical (radial) direction

[^rg-cd3a4587f5d3]: WB — well-balanced

[^rg-db3b2c69533d]: $\rho_{\mathrm{sf}}, p_{\mathrm{sf}}$ — face ("scan face") reference density and pressure; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp#L470-L476)

[^rg-5826c2f5cd26]: wb-wall-clamp — whether to clamp the well-balanced wall continuation

[^rg-e659dcc78f19]: non-hydrostatic — fraction of the vertical body force retained by the non-hydrostatic treatment

[^rg-f70527012078]: API — application programming interface
